material_definitions: Solid electrolytes based on lithium titanium phosphate (LiTi2(PO4)3) were prepared.
The materials studied involve partially replacing Ti4+ in LiTi2(PO4)3 with M3+ ions (M = Al, Cr, Ga, Fe, Sc, In, Lu, Y, and La) or P5+ with Si4+ ions.
The main material systems investigated were Li(1+x)Ti2SizP(3-x)O12 and Li(1+x)MxTi(2-x)(PO4)3.
This specific measurement corresponds to the maximum conductivity achieved in the Li(1+x)MxTi(2-x)(PO4)3 series for M = Al.
Solid electrolytes based on lithium titanium phosphate (LiTi2(PO4)3) were prepared.
The materials studied involve partially replacing Ti4+ in LiTi2(PO4)3 with M3+ ions (M = Al, Cr, Ga, Fe, Sc, In, Lu, Y, and La) or P5+ with Si4+ ions.
The main material systems investigated were Li(1+x)Ti2SizP(3-x)O12 and Li(1+x)MxTi(2-x)(PO4)3.
This specific measurement corresponds to the maximum conductivity achieved in the Li(1+x)MxTi(2-x)(PO4)3 series for M = Sc.
The Li(1+x)Ti2SixP(3-x)O12 solid electrolyte system was studied.
Samples were sintered at 1473 K for 2 hours.
The replacement of P5+ with Si4+ occurred, although unknown peaks appeared for the entire region.
Porosity decreased remarkably and conductivities were greatly enhanced with increasing Si4+ substitution.
The Li(1+x)MxTi(2-x)(PO4)3 systems are solid electrolytes based on LiTi2(PO4)3, where Ti4+ sites are partially substituted by various M3+ ions.
These systems are classified into single phase (M=Al, Cr, Ga, Fe, Sc, In) or mixed phase (M=Lu, Y, La).
Maximum conductivity was generally achieved around x=0.3.
The conductivity enhancement is primarily attributed to the increase of the sintered pellet density due to M3+ substitution.
The Li(1+x)MxTi(2-x)(PO4)3 systems are solid electrolytes based on LiTi2(PO4)3, where Ti4+ sites are partially substituted by various M3+ ions.
These systems are classified into single phase (M=Al, Cr, Ga, Fe, Sc, In) or mixed phase (M=Lu, Y, La).
Maximum conductivity was generally achieved around x=0.3.
The conductivity enhancement is primarily attributed to the increase of the sintered pellet density due to M3+ substitution.
LiTi2(PO4)3 had poor ionic conductivity and showed high porosity in the sintered pellets.
The partial substitution of the P5+ site with Si4+ or of the Ti4+ site with M3+ in the LiTi2(PO4)3 system was very effective for the enhancement of the conductivity.
Mixing binders such as Li2O or Li4P2O7 with LiTi2(PO4)3 is also successful in obtaining a high conductivity lithium ionic conductor.
The lithium ionic conductors based on lithium titanium phosphate are proved to be excellent solid electrolytes for their high lithium ionic conductivity even at room temperature.
